questions.question_text: Which division is equivalent to $1.736\div0.9$ with a whole-number divisor?

options.why: Multiplied only the divisor by $10$, leaving the dividend unchanged.
Multiplied only the dividend by $10$, so the divisor is still a decimal.
Multiplied the divisor by $100$ and left the dividend alone.

questions.solution_text:
The divisor $0.9$ has $1$ decimal place, so multiply both numbers by $10$.
$1.736\div0.9=17.36\div9$

questions.question_text: Which division is equivalent to $0.063\div0.03$ with a whole-number divisor?

options.why: Shifted the divisor two places but the dividend only one.
Shifted the dividend three places but the divisor only two.
Made the divisor whole without shifting the dividend at all.

questions.solution_text:
The divisor $0.03$ has $2$ decimal places, so multiply both numbers by $100$.
$0.063\div0.03=6.3\div3$

questions.question_text: Which division is equivalent to $0.08\div0.002$ with a whole-number divisor?

options.why: Shifted the divisor three places but the dividend only two.
Shifted the dividend four places but the divisor only three.
Made the divisor whole without shifting the dividend at all.

questions.solution_text:
The divisor $0.002$ has $3$ decimal places, so multiply both numbers by $1000$.
$0.08\div0.002=80\div2$

questions.question_text: Which division is equivalent to $287\div1.2$ with a whole-number divisor?

options.why: Multiplied the dividend by $10$ but left the divisor as the decimal $1.2$.
Multiplied the divisor by $10$ but moved the dividend's decimal point the wrong way, dividing $287$ by $10$.
Moved the dividend's decimal point the wrong way and left the divisor unchanged, so neither number is fixed.

questions.solution_text:
The divisor $1.2$ has $1$ decimal place, so multiply both numbers by $10$.
The whole-number dividend $287$ gains a zero.
$287\div1.2=2870\div12$
